title: The Hymn of the Robe of Glory
author: G. R. S. Mead
description: The Hymn of the Robe of Glory by G. R. S. Mead (London: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1908), Volume V of his 'Echoes from the Gnosis' series. The hymn, also known as the Hymn of the Pearl, is a Syriac poem preserved in the apocryphal Acts of Thomas, probably composed in the Edessan milieu of the second or third century. It tells of a royal prince sent from the East by his parents, the King of Kings and the Queen of the East, down into Egypt to recover a pearl guarded by a serpent. He forgets his mission in the foreign land until a letter from home awakens him; he charms the serpent, takes the pearl and returns to put on his radiant robe of glory, which reflects his true self. Mead provides an introduction and a translation with commentary interpreting the hymn as an allegory of the soul's descent, forgetting, awakening and return. It is one of the most beautiful expressions of Gnostic soteriology.
